runs.reason: The paper measures pointing error (deviation of initial movement direction from target), which is literally a magnitude of angular error - i.e., higher_more_error in raw semantics. However, per the outcome definition, this deviation after feedback removal reflects retained implicit recalibration (aftereffect), so a larger deviation corresponds to more adaptation/construct, making higher values 'better' for this outcome. The paper explicitly states the after-effect magnitude 'was similar in both age groups' / 'not degraded' in seniors, without stating which group's raw value was numerically greater, so direction_stated_in_text is unknown.
